messages.subject: D-RUG (10am-noon) and Tea Time (1-2pm) Thursday this week
messages.subject_clean: D-RUG (10am-noon) and Tea Time (1-2pm) Thursday this week
messages.body_plain:
Hi D-RUGgies!

We will be meeting this Thursday from 10-noon virtually and in person in the DataLab classroom (Library 360). This is a group working session so come with your questions for our expeRts, or just bring your laptop and get in some distraction free R-coding time. Additionally, if there are topics you would like to see someone do a deeper dive on, let us know!

There is also Tea Time in the DataLab classroom from 1-2pm Thursday if you are looking to take a break from work with tea (or coffee) and cookies.

Zoom at this link: https://ucdavis.zoom.us/j/96397082218?pwd=S0JXcW5hcUFkbTcwMHFQV1NVNkg3Zz09

Please consider posting your questions to our Discourse <https://d-rug.discourse.group/> site in advance of attending D-RUG virtually. This helps us do a better job of answering your questions, and also keep a log of the types of questions we see frequently.

See you then,

Your D-RUG Coo[R]dinators

messages.subject: Opportunity for new D-RUG coordinator(s)!
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

D-RUG <https://d-rug.github.io/> is looking for additional student organizers to join our coo[R]dinating team! This is a great opportunity for folks looking to gain experience helping others with R or learning new skills alongside other R users. You don't need to be an expert in R - we welcome all experience levels. The commitment involves attending as many D-RUG meetings as you can (Thursdays from 10 - 12 pm in Shields 360), assisting with other activities as you'd like (e.g., D-RUG marketing, workshops, etc), and/or leading engagement activities with R-users on campus. If you're interested, please reply to this message!

Thanks,
Your D-RUG Coordinators

What is D-RUG exactly? The Davis R Users' Group is a weekly working group to get some help with R-specific coding problems. Sponsored by the UC Davis Datalab <https://datalab.ucdavis.edu/>, the coordinators include UCD data scientists as well as grad students on campus. We meet for 2 hours in an open-forum format so you can make the time what you want it to be whether that's co-working, asking questions, or meeting other R users.

messages.subject: FW: Join us at the #maptimeDavis Lightning Talk session! Sign up now!
messages.subject_clean: Join us at the #maptimeDavis Lightning Talk session! Sign up now!
messages.body_plain:
D-RUG members are invited to participate in #maptimeDavis’ Lightning Talk (show-and-tell) session! If you’re working with spatial data, consider presenting.

Michele Tobias, PhD

Geospatial Data Specialist

DataLab: Data Science & Informatics

UC Davis Library

370 Shields Library

(530)752-7532

mmto...@ucdavis.edu

ORCID: 0000-0002-2954-8710 <https://orcid.org/0000-0002-2954-8710>

Pronouns: she, her, hers

From: geospatia...@ucdavis.edu <geospatia...@ucdavis.edu> On Behalf Of Lauren Mabe
Sent: Wednesday, October 23, 2024 1:03 PM
To: geographystudent Sympa List <geograph...@ucdavis.edu>; geospatial Sympa List <geosp...@ucdavis.edu>
Subject: [geospatial] [#maptimeDavis] Join us at the #maptimeDavis Lightning Talk session! Sign up now!

Have you recently made an interesting map for your research? Collected a new spatial dataset? Taken an epic drone pic? Drawn a cool map for your D&D campaign? If so, then you should sign up for the 2024 #maptimeDavis Lightning Talk session!

What is a lightning talk session? Think of it like a show-and-tell of all things geospatial, cartographic, GIS, and more! Each speaker will have 5 minutes to share what they've been working on, think of it like a mapping show-and-tell. Anything that can spark discussion and collaboration across the UC Davis geospatial community is welcome! Anyone who is working on (or thinking about) a project involving spatial data – undergraduates, graduate students, postdocs, staff, faculty, and community members are encouraged to join us. This is a great time to share your progress, get new ideas, or learn more about research happening on campus :)

If you are interested in doing a lightning talk, please use this form <https://forms.gle/2s7K2DAJmcmWeKsU6> to sign up. The lightning talk session will be held on Friday, November 1st from 10am-12 in the the  Physical and Data Sciences Building <https://campusmap.ucdavis.edu/?b=115>, previously known as PSEL (Physical Sciences & Engineering Library), Seminar Room (room 1025).

If you have any questions/comments/concerns, please reach out to Lauren Mabe at lm...@ucdavis.edu

--

Lauren Mabe

Ph.D. Candidate | Geography Graduate Group
University of California, Davis

she/her
